2_Introduction: The PCE devices reached 23.1922% and featured a VOC of 1.1563 V, FF of 80.6915%, and short-circuit current density (JSC) of 24.857 mA/cm². The composition of the 1.73 mol/L perovskite film is Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. Specifically, the perovskite precursor solution was first deposited at 1000 rpm for 10 s, and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. At the last 10 s, 160 µL of CB solution was dropped on the perovskite. By subjecting the film to 110 °C for 25 min, the perovskite lattice attained its ideal orientation.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—engineered with a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture exhibiting an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppressed halide vacancy formation energy—undergoes kinetically controlled crystallization wherein the dual-speed spin-coating (1000 rpm for nucleation, 5000 rpm for lateral confinement) coupled with precisely timed CB antisolvent quenching at the final 10 s critically modulates intermediate solvate phase stability, suppresses uncontrolled Ostwald ripening, and promotes vertical grain alignment; this sequence minimizes interfacial trap states at grain boundaries and reduces Pb⁰/PbI₂-related deep-level defects, while the 110 °C, 25 min thermal annealing drives complete solvent evaporation, relieves lattice strain evidenced by narrowed XRD (001) peak FWHM and absence of residual PbI₂ at 12.6°, and locks in a thermodynamically favored α-phase with enhanced octahedral connectivity and reduced I⁻ migration propensity—collectively yielding high phase purity, low non-radiative recombination, and improved charge-carrier diffusion length. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in the formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the FA-rich, Cs/MA-doped lattice synergistically stabilizes the B–X octahedral framework against dynamic distortion, while the stoichiometric excess of iodide (reflected in the X = 3.0 stoichiometry) passivates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites at surfaces and grain edges, and the controlled crystallization kinetics inherently limit halide segregation and interstitial vacancy accumulation—mechanisms further corroborated by uniform film coverage and high grayscale homogeneity in optical micrographs, intense and spatially homogeneous photoluminescence emission with monoexponential decay kinetics τ ≈ 1.2 µs indicating suppressed trap-assisted recombination, and sharp, symmetric XRD reflections confirming minimal microstrain and absence of δ-phase or 2D interlayers. These morphologically, optically, and structurally validated improvements in crystallinity, interfacial order, and bulk defect suppression directly translate into superior charge extraction, minimized voltage losses, and reduced series resistance, culminating in a VOC of 1.1563 V, JSC of 24.857 mA/cm², FF of 80.6915%, and PCE of 23.1922%.
